extracted.intended_audience: federal agency staff, agency hearing examiners, administrative lawyers, and policymakers involved in administrative procedure and rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria for federal administrative procedures, especially hearing-examiner processes, agency rulemaking, attorney recognition/discipline, and associated statistical metrics for assessing backlog and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office is charged to study continuously the adequacy of procedures, to develop uniform, simple, and economical procedures, and to assist departments and agencies in the formulation and improvement of specific procedures so that public business may be conducted fairly with economy, efficiency, and dispatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts as a clearinghouse for procedural information; works by informal face-to-face meetings, intradepartmental studies, rulemaking studies, and special assignments to stimulate adoption of uniform practice across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of Procedural Legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing procedural provisions of proposed legislation, determine whether the proposed procedures are lawful in the constitutional sense, whether they conform to the pattern of the Administrative Procedure Act, and whether they are uniform with other procedures in the same field and related fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also inquire whether procedures are fair to the government, the public, and regulated persons; whether they are clear and simple; and whether they are designed to accomplish regulatory purpose with economy and dispatch. If defects exist, informal conference with agency staff may be sought and proposals may be revised before Department of Justice comment to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of Agency Machinery for Continuous Procedural Study
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should have official or staff committees charged with continuous study of agency procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of such committees correlates with greater use of President's Conference recommendations; the Office surveyed agencies to determine presence and activity of such machinery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of President's Conference Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should consider and, where practicable, put into effect the procedural recommendations of the President's Conference on Administrative Procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure use by whether agencies have applied recommendations in rule changes or in aggregate informal improvements; the Office surveyed agencies for such adoption and utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of Attorneys to Practice Before Agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed uniform rule: any person who is a member in good standing of the bar of the Supreme Court of the United States or of the highest court of any State, Territory, or the District of Columbia, and is not under any court order restricting practice, may represent others before the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text of the proposed rule circulated to agencies (Appendix); many agencies have adopted or rewritten rules in substance to follow the proposal; agencies may still require further proof of authority in particular cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service Upon Attorneys When Representation Is Known in Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: When any participant is represented by a lawyer and that fact is made known in writing to the agency, service of any notice or other written communication shall be upon the lawyer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where statute prescribes another method of service, that statutory method also applies; if multiple attorneys represent a participant, service on any one suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform Agency Rules for Discipline of Attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should provide simple, adequate, and uniform rules for discipline of attorneys guilty of misconduct or failing to meet high standards of professional integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office prepared a tabulation of existing agency rules (Appendix) and is studying measures to improve and make uniform such disciplinary provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing Procedures Evaluation Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the adequacy, efficiency, and uniformity of agency procedures for the conduct of administrative hearings, including official notice, service of process, subpoenas, depositions and interrogatories, and prehearing conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts identifying salient features of agency rules on each subject are published in the Appendix together with President's Conference illustrative rules; work can involve major code revisions or drafting single rules for specific agency matters (examples: FCC revisions, Post Office deposition rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Proceeding' for Reporting Purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the Office's hearing statistics, a 'proceeding' means a matter referred to an examiner for hearing and decision by him even though it may involve several petitions, applications, claimants, or docket numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A consolidated proceeding resolved by one joint hearing and a single decision is reported as one proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of Proceedings into Types
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are asked to assort proceedings into types according to similarities and differences in scope, function, relief available, complexity, and statutory or regulatory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The division of types provided by agencies is used in the statistical tables, with some character-name abbreviations for reporting convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing-Examiner Statistical Metrics (Backlog and Volume)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and publish facts and statistics on proceedings pending before examiners: number pending at start, new cases assigned, cases remanded/reassigned in the year, examiners' total output, and number pending at end of year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nine statistical tables present backlog, volume, age, manner of disposition, use of shortened procedures, length of stages, and examiner staffing; comparisons among agencies should account for significant differences in types of proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of Disposition Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Report how proceedings were terminated: decision on the merits, dismissal on procedural grounds, voluntary withdrawal, removal from examiner to agency action, and other modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table II reports the distribution (e.g., approximately 78.8% of dispositions were decisions on the merits in fiscal 1957).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age and Time-to-Event Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure age of proceedings from date of assignment to examiner, and measure time intervals such as assignment-to-decision, assignment-to-opening-of-hearing, length of hearings, time from close of hearing to final submission, and from final submission to issuance of examiner's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables VI–VIII present these intervals; data completeness varies by agency and sampling adjustments used where full data unavailable (e.g., ICC 6-month sampling, Social Security sampling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'Shortened Procedures' (Decisions Without Evidentiary Hearings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report and evaluate extent of use of shortened procedures that permit examiners to issue decisions on the merits without evidentiary hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare time involved in shortened-procedure dispositions versus regular hearing cases; shortened procedures are often used for convenience where oral hearing is unnecessary and to reduce travel, transcript costs, etc. (examples: ICC, CAB statistics and comparisons reported).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing Conferences — Purpose and Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Prehearing conferences may be used to formulate issues, prepare for hearing, limit matters in dispute, and otherwise streamline proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies vary on initiation (presiding officer may request, parties may suggest) and use; some statutes or agency rules allow written suggestions or correspondence in lieu of personal attendance; charts in Appendix list agency practices and specific citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions — Notice, Officer Qualifications, Recordation, Signing, Attestation, Return
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositions require notice specifying time/place/witness; officer before whom deposition is to be taken must be qualified to administer oaths; officer must put witness on oath and personally or by designee record testimony (typewriter, stenographer, tape); objections must be noted; transcription must be submitted to witness for examination and signing; officer certifies and returns deposition to agency Secretary for filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsigned depositions may be used unless a motion to suppress succeeds; party taking deposition must notify others of filing; fees for deponents and officers follow District Court rates and are paid by the taking party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions Upon Interrogatories
rubrics_metrics.description: Where depositions are taken on written interrogatories, each interrogatory must be numbered and filed with notice stating deponent and officer; parties have specified time windows to serve cross- and redirect-interrogatories; officer administers oath and records each interrogatory and answer serially; officer certifies and returns originals to Agency Secretary and copies to counsel and deponent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Otherwise governed by general deposition rule; strict limits on who may be present during interrogatory deposition (only deponent, officer, reporter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Notice — Matters of Law and Material Facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency or hearing officer may officially notice matters of law (e.g., Constitution, federal statutes, federal court decisions, Federal Register materials, state laws, governmental organization) and material facts (e.g., pendency and disposition of agency proceedings, general business customs, notorious facts, technical knowledge within agency expertise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: any party may request official notice; a fact officially noticed and used in decision must be clearly and precisely stated in the decision; parties may controvert official notice when made or afterwards by exceptions or petitions for reconsideration and must state supporting sources and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for Admission/Recognition of Attorneys Before Agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies' rules vary: some require application, certificate of court, or examination; the proposed uniform rule would dispense with formal admission procedures and rely on bar membership in a highest court as the qualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix tables enumerate which agencies required application, certificates, or exams as of Dec 31, 1957; some agencies have eliminated application requirements (e.g., Subversive Activities Control Board after Jan 1958).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature/Appearance as Certificate of Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: When a person appears or signs in practice before an agency, the personal appearance or signature shall constitute a representation to the agency that he is authorized and qualified to represent the party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency may require further proof of authority to act in a representative capacity; signature can operate as certification absent contrary evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by or Upon Attorneys — Specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: When a participant is represented by an attorney and that fact is in writing to the agency, notices or communications required or permitted to be given to or by the participant shall be given to or by such attorney; if multiple attorneys represent a participant, service on any one constitutes sufficient service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If another method of service is specifically provided by statute, that method must also be used; the proposed rule embodies the substance of rules prevailing before many agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions on Disbarment of Attorneys — Grounds and Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency rules may provide grounds for suspension or disbarment including conviction, being 'unfit' or failing to meet agency standards of conduct, violation of stated rules, or disbarment by courts or other administrative agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables in Appendix list agency practices: whether notice must be given, whether a hearing is afforded, whether suspension may be by summary order or after hearing, and cross-recognition of disbarment by other courts or agencies; procedures and prerequisites vary by agency.
